questions.question: Simplify (6x² − 10x) ÷ 2x and explain the law used.
questions.expected_answer: The distributive law for division: each term on top is divided by 2x. 6x² ÷ 2x = 3x and −10x ÷ 2x = −5, so the answer is 3x − 5. Check: 2x(3x − 5) = 6x² − 10x.

questions.question: Why is (9a³ − 6a² + 3a) ÷ 3a equal to 3a² − 2a + 1 and not 3a² − 2a?
questions.expected_answer: The third term 3a ÷ 3a is 1, not 0; a quantity divided by itself is one. Dropping it is the commonest error. Multiplying back without the +1 gives 9a³ − 6a² with no 3a, so the +1 is needed.

questions.question: Why may x be cancelled in (6x² − 10x)/(2x) but not in (x + 5)/x?
questions.expected_answer: In the first, x is a factor of every term on top, so it cancels from each. In the second, x is one term of a sum, not a factor of the whole top; cancelling it would be cancelling a term. (x + 5)/x = 1 + 5/x.
